**Svær ileus** (severe ileus) is a serious acute surgical condition characterized by a critical need for early medical intervention. In the context of acute care, it defines a specific subgroup of patients for whom the timing of antibiotic treatment is exceptionally urgent. Prompt administration of antibiotics is essential to reduce physiological stress and prevent severe complications [^src1].

Within the Danish healthcare system, severe ileus is recognized as a life-threatening acute surgical emergency. According to the January 2026 draft of the Akut Kirurgi Databasen (Acute Surgery Database), clinical guidelines mandate that antibiotic therapy be initiated as quickly as possible for patients suspected of having severe ileus, alongside other critical conditions like perforated hollow organs and ischemia. Crucially, this immediate treatment protocol applies regardless of whether the patient presents with a fever or altered infection markers [^src1].

The management of severe ileus is deeply embedded in a broader national quality improvement initiative led by the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut). The condition is a primary focus of systematic monitoring programs designed to ensure early diagnosis and treatment. Specifically, it is tied to Quality Indicator 1, which tracks the administration of antibiotics within a three-hour window. Efforts to optimize care for severe ileus patients also address practical clinical barriers, such as the tendency to prioritize CT scans (Quality Indicator 2) over the immediate delivery of antibiotics, drawing on evidence from clinical studies like AHA and ELPQUICK to refine political and developmental time targets [^src1].
